harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Implemented an Ansible playbook (run from node4, the designated control node) that publishes node2's private port-8080 app through node1 (VyOS router) so node3 can reach it, without exposing the rest of the node1<->node2 private network to node3. The private link (node1 eth1 <-> node2 ens7, previously unaddressed) was given static IPs 10.50.50.1/24 and 10.50.50.2/24; node2 got a minimal HTTP app bound only to its private IP; node1 got destination NAT (eth0:8080 -> 10.50.50.2:8080) plus hairpin source NAT (masquerade on eth1) so replies route back through the router, and a default-drop forward firewall with one narrow allow rule so no other port/host on the private network is reachable from node3. Verified node3 can reach the app via node1:8080 but gets 'No route to host' hitting node2's private IP directly. Diagnosed and worked around two real defects in this environment: the vyos.vyos collection's network_cli connection silently failed to persist VyOS commits, and vyos's default vbash login shell drops VyOS config-session state when SSH runs a nested plain bash -c. Fixed by using Ansible's raw module with 'sudo bash -c' (vyos has NOPASSWD ALL sudo) to run the native configure/set/commit/save sequence directly as root, verified via new commit revisions and config.boot content. Completed the mandatory restart protocol: captured boot_id and functional baselines on all four nodes, restarted them one at a time via systemctl reboot, polled until exec was available again, confirmed each node's boot_id changed, and verified full recovery (NAT/firewall config, private IPs, app service, and the node3->node1->node2 path) after every restart.
actions_performed: Surveyed topology on all 4 nodes: node1=VyOS (eth0 mgmt/10.100.201.10, eth1 private unaddressed), node2=Ubuntu16.04 (ens2 mgmt/10.100.201.11, ens7 private unaddressed), node3=Ubuntu16.04 client (10.100.201.12), node4=Ubuntu24.04 Ansible control node (10.100.201.13)
Bootstrapped Ansible SSH access: added node4's id_rsa.pub to node2/node3 antrieb user and node1 vyos user authorized_keys
Installed vyos.vyos Ansible collection on node4

Wrote /root/pf-ansible/site.yml (3 plays: configure node2's private IP+app via raw module for legacy Python 3.5 target, configure node1 NAT/firewall via VyOS raw configure/commit/save, verify from node3) and inventory.ini
Diagnosed vyos_config module commit-not-persisting bug (kernel nftables applied but config tree/config.boot unchanged) by comparing manual CLI runs vs ansible runs
Diagnosed vbash-vs-bash config-session loss when SSH'ing as vyos user directly; fixed by adding 'sudo' before 'bash -c' in the raw tasks

Ran the full playbook end-to-end successfully: node2 got static 10.50.50.2/24 on ens7 + private-app.service on 8080; node1 got 10.50.50.1/24 on eth1 + DNAT + hairpin SNAT + default-drop forward firewall with narrow allow
Verified functionality: node3 curl to node1:8080 returns app content; node3 curl to node2's private IP fails with No route to host
Captured pre-restart baselines (boot_id, service state, NAT rules, IPs) on all 4 nodes
Restarted node1 via systemctl reboot, polled until exec available, confirmed new boot_id and full config/NAT/app recovery
Restarted node2, confirmed new boot_id, private-app.service active, ens7 IP restored, end-to-end curl works
Restarted node3, confirmed new boot_id, end-to-end curl via node1 works and direct private-IP access still blocked
Restarted node4, confirmed new boot_id, ansible tooling and SSH access intact
Cleaned up temporary root SSH key added to node1 during diagnosis and leftover test files on node4
